name: Hanko
title: Ship Thickness Measurement Hanko | Ro-Ro & Winter Port UTM
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Hanko for ro-ro freighters, ro-pax and car carriers: vehicle deck, ramp, ballast tank and hull gauging through the year.
h1: Thickness Gauging for Ro-Ro, Ro-Pax and Car Carriers at the Port of Hanko
intro: Hanko, on the peninsula at Finland's southernmost tip, has served as the country's winter port since the nineteenth century, because the sea here usually freezes late and clears early. Today it is a fast ro-ro and car-import harbour, with liner services across the Baltic and car carriers bringing in new vehicles. Ships turn around quickly, so gauging is planned around lay periods and gaps in the cargo work. The Atlantis crew travels to Hanko from India for every job.

highlights.p: Hanko's position at the mouth of the Gulf of Finland gives it lighter ice than the ports further east or north. Ships still need ice class in hard winters, but open-deck work and launch transfers are possible on more days of the year here.

Hanko became Finland's largest semi-trailer port in 2025. Trailer decks, lashing points and ramps on these ro-ro freighters take heavy wear, and gauging is slotted into weekend gaps, lay days or delayed departures on their fixed rotations.

highlights.h: Car carriers in the Baltic trade
highlights.p: Car carriers deliver new vehicles into Finland through Hanko. Between discharge and the next loading, empty decks give a team access to deck plating, hoistable-deck supports and ramps, with crack detection at the details that carry repeated loads.

port.h: The Port of Hanko and its liner traffic
p: The Port of Hanko sits at the end of the Hanko peninsula, where the Gulf of Finland opens into the main body of the Baltic. It works through three harbours: the Western Harbour beside the town, which carries the bulk of the ro-ro and cargo traffic; the Outer Harbour; and Koverhar, a former steelworks harbour further up the peninsula that now handles industrial cargo. The port's reputation rests on fast liner traffic. Ro-ro and ro-pax freight services, with Finnlines and Transfennica among the operators, connect Hanko with Poland and other continental ports, carrying semi-trailers, containers and industrial goods, while car carriers bring in new vehicles for distribution across Finland. Exports through the port include forest and technology-industry products, much of it moving in trailers and containers on the same ships.

Ice explains much of Hanko's history. The southern tip of Finland faces open sea, and in most winters the ice arrives here later and leaves sooner than in the eastern Gulf of Finland or the Bothnian Sea, so Hanko was developed with a railway connection as a port that could keep Finnish trade moving through the winter. Ice still forms in hard years, Finnish winter traffic restrictions still apply, and the regular ro-ro tonnage is ice-classed, but the season is shorter and the ice usually lighter than at Kotka or Oulu. For a gauging crew that widens the window for launch work and anything done on open decks, and it means ice-belt wear on Hanko-route ships often comes from voyages to icier ports as much as from Hanko itself.

Ro-ro calls are short and frequent. A freighter on a fixed rotation can be discharged and reloaded within the same day, and weekly services leave little idle time, so the realistic gauging windows are weekend lay-overs, scheduled lay days and the gaps that open when a departure is held back. Car carriers stay for as long as their discharge plan takes and may also load export units, which gives clearer access to empty decks for a few hours at a time. Koverhar handles bulk and break-bulk ships whose stays are longer and less tightly timed. Ships arriving early or waiting for a slot anchor in the approaches, which can be exposed to open-sea weather, so launch work there depends on the day.

The Western Harbour is where most of the work happens. On ro-ro freighters and ro-pax ships we measure main-deck and tank-top plating in the trailer lanes, the areas around lashing points, internal ramps and the stern ramp, working deck by deck as the ship empties and stopping cleanly when loading resumes. Ballast tanks and voids are entered only after the crew has ventilated them and issued an entry permit, so tank work is planned for the longest window in the rotation. Car carriers at the car-import berths give access to car decks between discharge and loading, with the ship lighting the hoistable decks for the team.

Koverhar suits longer jobs on bulk and general cargo ships, where holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks can be measured over a stay that is not governed by a liner timetable. Hanko has no dry dock for merchant ships; the nearest Finnish docking yards are Turku Repair Yard at Naantali and the shipyard at Rauma, and many ro-ro owners dock at yards around the Baltic. Readings from a Hanko call give that yard and the class surveyor a measured starting point, and help the owner decide which tanks and decks must be opened during the dock period.
list: Western Harbour ro-ro berths — trailer-lane decks, lashing areas and ramps on ro-ro freighters during lay days or weekend lay-overs
Car-import berths — car-deck plating, hoistable-deck supports and ramps on car carriers between discharge and loading
Ro-pax berths — vehicle decks, voids and ballast tanks gauged in stages on ships that cannot leave their rotation
Koverhar Harbour — holds, hatch covers and tanks on bulk and break-bulk ships with longer, less timetabled stays
Anchorage in the Hanko approaches — launch-borne jobs on ships waiting for a berth, weather permitting

context.h: Inspection, regulation and trade patterns at Hanko
p: Finland applies Paris MoU port state control through Traficom, the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency, and in a ro-ro port with frequent calls the same ships are seen again and again, so a structural deficiency recorded once tends to be followed up on later visits. On ro-ro and ro-pax ships, inspectors pay close attention to bow and stern doors, ramps and the watertight and weathertight integrity of the hull, which makes wastage and cracking around those openings a practical concern as well as a class item. Hanko's liner services run between EU ports, so their emissions fall wholly within the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime, and the operators' fleet decisions, whether to replace older tonnage or keep it with steel renewal, rest on the condition data their superintendents collect.

Car carriers raise questions of their own. Battery-electric cars weigh more than the models many car decks were designed around, and they burn differently, so owners of older car carriers are reviewing deck strength and the state of their hoistable decks with that trade in mind. Ice class still matters at Hanko in hard winters, and under the Finnish-Swedish Ice Class Rules the ice belt must keep its scantlings for the ship to keep its class notation. Ships on year-round Baltic rotations collect ice abrasion across many ports, and Hanko's milder conditions often make it the convenient place to measure what those voyages have taken.

jobs.h: Thickness gauging jobs typical of Hanko
jobs.p: Hanko jobs are shaped by the liner timetable. Superintendents of ro-ro and ro-pax ships usually split a renewal-survey scope across several calls, measuring one deck or group of tanks each time, and keep the bottom and the full tank programme for the dry dock. Car carrier owners ask for car-deck and ramp readings with crack detection between discharge and loading. Bulk and break-bulk ships at Koverhar bring more conventional hold and tank scopes. Because Hanko's ice season is shorter, launch transfers to the anchorage and work on open decks are possible for more of the year than at many Finnish ports, which helps when a job cannot wait for spring.
list: Main-deck and tank-top plating in the trailer lanes of a ro-ro freighter during a weekend lay-over at the Western Harbour
Car-deck, hoistable-deck support and ramp gauging with MPI on a car carrier between discharge and export loading
Ballast tank and void-space readings on a ro-pax, split across two lay days ahead of an intermediate survey
Hold, hatch-cover and ballast tank gauging on a bulk carrier lying at Koverhar
Pre-docking steel estimate on an ice-class ro-ro before its dry-docking elsewhere in the Baltic
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping checks on a ro-ro freighter during a scheduled lay day

logistics: Helsinki-Vantaa is the nearest international airport, and the team continues by road west along the coast to the Hanko peninsula. Access to the Western Harbour, the Outer Harbour and Koverhar is arranged by the ship's agent, including ISPS passes and, for ships at anchor, a launch. Our technicians come from India and need a Schengen visa for Finland; because Hanko windows are short, we tie mobilisation to a confirmed lay day or call, keep the agent updated on travel, and build consular processing into the plan.

faqs.q: How much can be gauged on a ro-ro freighter during a Hanko turnaround?
faqs.a: On a same-day turnaround, little beyond a focused deck or piping check. The useful windows are lay days, weekend lay-overs and delayed departures, when a deck can be measured empty and one or two ballast tanks ventilated in advance. We usually plan a renewal-survey scope across several such windows and leave the bottom and remaining tanks for the dry dock.

faqs.q: Is Hanko easier to work in during winter than other Finnish ports?
faqs.a: Often, because the ice season at Finland's southern tip is usually shorter and lighter than in the eastern Gulf or the Bothnian Sea, so launches to the anchorage and work on open decks are possible on more days. Winter traffic restrictions and ice can still apply in a hard year, so we keep a margin in the schedule and plan any external readings for milder weather.

faqs.q: Can you work on car carriers at Hanko?
faqs.a: Yes, between discharge and loading, when the decks are clear and the ship can light the hoistable decks. Car-deck plating, stiffeners, hoistable-deck supports and ramps form the usual scope, with magnetic particle testing at supports and hinges where cracking is suspected. Ballast tanks can be added if the crew prepares them in advance, and priorities are agreed beforehand so the key areas come first.

Hanko has no merchant dry dock. Finnish options include Turku Repair Yard at Naantali and the Rauma shipyard, and many ro-ro operators dock in Poland, Germany or elsewhere on the Baltic. Readings taken during a Hanko call carry the thickness measurement plan references, so the docking yard and the surveyor can use them to order steel and plan the close-up survey before the ship arrives.
